claim: Ice is less dense than liquid water because its hydrogen-bonded lattice holds molecules farther apart.

beats.caption: Most solids get denser when they freeze.
beats.vo: Most solids get denser when they freeze, so their solid form sinks in their own liquid. Water breaks that pattern.

beats.caption: Hydrogen bonds hold water in an open lattice.
beats.vo: As water cools, hydrogen bonds pull molecules into a hexagonal lattice. That lattice holds them farther apart than in liquid water, so ice takes up more space for the same mass.

beats.caption: Less dense, so it floats. Lakes freeze from the top.
beats.vo: Less dense means ice floats. The layer on top insulates the water below, so lakes freeze from the top down and fish survive winter.

sources.text: Eisenberg & Kauzmann, The Structure and Properties of Water (Oxford University Press, 1969)
